headline: Sequence foundation models extend across DNA, RNA and protein as evaluation rigor tightens
label: Sequence Foundation Model Reliability
summary: New RNA and DNA pretraining schemes arrive alongside leakage-controlled benchmarks and conformal calibration that test how far PLM-derived predictions can be trusted.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretraining sequence representations and reusing them downstream. For nucleic acids, structRFM pretrains on 21M sequence-structure pairs, LIMBER combines self-attention with Mamba over 40.5M ncRNA sequences, and IsoAlign pretrains DNA models through isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment with JEPA objectives. TriTower-m6Am fuses RNA-FM embeddings with BiLSTM and RGCN towers. On proteins, MaskNGly predicts N-glycosylation sites zero-shot from PLM embeddings, and PALM adapts ESM2 with LoRA and a BiLSTM for domain, functional-site and missense-effect prediction. The newer emphasis is reliability. Protify reports task dependence and homology leakage in PLM benchmarks. A separate study builds leakage-controlled benchmarks for variant effect predictors and a gradient-boosting consensus model. PPI-Caliper uses conformal calibration to control false discovery rate on PLM interaction scores without retraining. A MET kinase deep mutational scanning benchmark across 11 inhibitors finds current models largely ligand-invariant.
